6. Keep your budget in mind (16 model calls): combine tests into one run_python call where possible. Reserve at least 2 calls for final testing and submission. Submit only the program that passed the checks in steps 4a-4c.
7. Hard rule: never call submit before at least one run_tests call on the final code has passed all public examples. Submitting untested code (e.g. after 2 model calls with zero test runs) has repeatedly failed on hidden tests.
8. For optimization problems ("minimize", "maximize", "minimum cost"), the brute-force comparison must check the objective value, not only feasibility. Also check that the sample outputs match exactly, including whether the path/cost counts the start and end values as the statement says. Do not trust a model that claims correctness without running these checks.
9. Watch for edge cases the samples do not cover: n=1 or single-element inputs, disconnected or isolated components, zero or empty input (M=0), values equal to 0 or the maximum, forbidden or impossible states at the start or end, and whether the start state itself must satisfy the constraints. Include these in the brute-force cases.
10. Interpreting the statement: when several answers are accepted, still print the same sample-like format; when the output is a sequence, make sure the length and order match the statement exactly.
